analysis.title: Ignite Takeaways: Building for Broader Enterprise AI Demand
key_insights: Morgan Stanley met CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood at Ignite in San Francisco and stays Overweight on Microsoft, calling it one of the few enterprise AI companies already generating returns on its AI investments.

Management frames capacity allocation as a portfolio decision across GPUaaS contracts, first-party applications, Foundry and other enterprise workloads. Microsoft could commit more capacity under long-term contracts but does not treat maximizing those commitments as the objective.

Neocloud strategy is unchanged. Microsoft prefers owned facilities, then long-term leases where it controls fit-out, networking and equipment. Management attributed some deal cancellations to suppliers missing service-level commitments, and MS does not read this as a change in supply or demand.

Capacity gains come from CPU utilization and storage as well as GPUs, and new deployments include the same efficiency assumptions. MS says these gains should not be treated as a separate source of upside to capacity plans.

Management targets higher gross margins within Azure and M365 individually, and treats the reported Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage as an outcome. Faster Azure growth can keep diluting the blended Cloud margin while product-level margins improve.

Management stressed the system around the model (context, harness, memory, trust) and routing each task to the lowest-cost effective model. It sees frontier models for frontier problems, plus specialized MAI and open-weight models where they cost less. Microsoft IQ combines Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ.

One large customer's Cowork spending exceeded its spending on Microsoft's other products combined. CFO meetings cautioned that this is not representative, and that the products and sales motion are too new to give an adoption timeline. Coding adoption is strong and broader knowledge-work consumption is still early.

Agent 365 Business Analytics and Cost Management tie spending to adoption and outcomes, with budgeting policies and alerts. MS says the revenue benefit depends on how fast customers expand production workloads.

Maia custom silicon is positioned within a diversified sourcing strategy, like the earlier move from Intel to AMD and Cobalt. Microsoft cited up to 50% better performance for Cobalt 200 vs Cobalt 100 for agentic AI workflows.
MS price target is $650 (26x base case FY28e EPS of $24.41) against a $508.29 close on Nov 18, 2026. Bull case is $800 and bear case is $300.

market_movers.rationale: Management discussions at Ignite reinforced confidence in capacity allocation, product-level margin improvement and broader consumption monetization. Base case is 26x FY28e EPS of $24.41.

sector_views.rationale: MS industry view is Attractive, and it calls Microsoft one of the few AI winners in software.

earnings_insights: MS FY28e EPS is $24.41 (base case) and FY27e EPS is $19.86. Consensus (Refinitiv) is $23.97 for FY28e and $20.05 for FY27e.
Fiscal Q1 2027 EPS was reported at $4.92 (marked actual in the table). MS estimates are $4.87 for Q2, $4.96 for Q3 and $5.12 for Q4 of fiscal 2027.
MS FY27e revenue estimate is $398,980mm vs consensus $396,103mm, and net income is $147,354mm vs consensus $149,111mm.
risk_factors: Pace of Copilot and Cowork adoption outside coding is uncertain.
vol_and_positioning: Options-implied risk-neutral probabilities as of Nov 18, 2026 over 12 months: about 4.6% of the stock exceeding $800, about 20.3% exceeding $650, and about 8.9% falling below $300.
Hedge fund sector long/short ratio is 2.2x and sector net exposure is 30.6%. Institutional owners are 52.4% active.

tension_points.bull_case: Capacity-driven Azure growth inflection and Copilot monetization support high-teens revenue growth, with operating leverage offsetting gross margin pressure to give 20%+ EBIT growth and above 20% EPS growth.
tension_points.bear_case: Azure growth keeps decelerating at scale, M365 reaches penetration and AI Copilot adoption stays limited, giving mid-teens revenue growth and operating margins of only about 45.0% by FY28.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bear case: FY28 EPS of about $22 and operating margin of about 45.0% by FY28 from gross margin pressure.
